name: Hotbar Abilities
description: The active-skill layer that turns a basic attack into a build. Each slot binds an ability definition — cooldown, resource cost, targeting mode — and this component owns only the slot lifecycle: is it off cooldown, can the resource be paid, and when does it fire. The moment an ability connects it hands a damage packet to combat.damage_resolver, because a second place where damage numbers are computed is a place where balance patches land twice. Ongoing effects an ability leaves behind are combat.status_effects' problem — a burn that ticks for five seconds is status, not hotbar — and passive gear bonuses never pass through here either, since combat.equipment_slots applies those directly. What this component pointedly refuses to own is the UI: ui.hud renders the slots off the same cooldown events, so the hotbar runs headless in tests.

inputs.name: slots
inputs.description: How many ability slots the bar exposes. Six is the ARPG convention: enough for a build identity, few enough that every slot is a choice rather than a filing cabinet.

inputs.name: globalCooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Minimum gap between any two casts. Exists so macro-speed casting cannot fire six skills in one frame; per-ability cooldowns stack on top of this.

inputs.name: resourceRefundOnInterrupt
inputs.description: Whether an interrupted cast returns its resource cost. Refunding reads as generous; not refunding makes interrupts a real counter-play tool. False is the safer default.

inputs.name: allowMoveCast
inputs.description: Whether casting roots the caster. Rooting during a cast is the classic risk/reward dial; mobility builds set this true and pay for it elsewhere.

outputs.name: activeCooldowns
outputs.description: Per-slot seconds remaining, in slot order.

outputs.name: lastCastAbilityId
outputs.description: Most recent successful cast, for combo and telemetry consumers.
